summary: Sierra Leone admits ECOWAS citizens and 15 other nationalities (among them Kenya, Singapore, Malaysia and Jamaica) without a visa, and issues nearly everyone else a visa on arrival (USD 80 in cash), with the official eVisa portal (evisa.sl) as the apply-ahead alternative — USD 25 there for African Union nationals.

notes: You need an export licence to leave Sierra Leone with precious stones, according to the UK Foreign Office; the Government of Canada says the licence is issued by the Ministry of Mines and Mineral Resources and warns of fraud, including fake export certificates. The UK Foreign Office says diamond smuggling carries heavy penalties, including prison.

payments.text: The Government of Canada describes Sierra Leone as a cash-based economy: credit cards are not widely accepted, there are very few ATMs in Freetown, and strict rules limit the import of foreign currency in cash. Exchange money only at banks or official foreign exchange offices — the US dollar and the euro are the easiest to exchange. The UK Foreign Office adds that many medical facilities, particularly outside Freetown, accept only cash.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says the political situation has improved since the civil war ended in 2002 but can change, and protests can turn violent, so avoid political gatherings and follow any curfews. It reports robberies of British nationals, sometimes at knifepoint, in parts of Freetown and at peninsula beach resorts, and advises completing road journeys in daylight. Canada says armed robberies, carjackings and burglaries have occurred in foreigners' homes, with a higher risk of serious crime after dark.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says the visa on arrival costs USD 80, paid in cash in US dollars. The official e-Visa portal is evisa.sl.

Lungi airport is across a wide estuary from Freetown — around 3 hours by road. The UK Foreign Office says the two main water taxi operators run a reliable 30–45 minute service timed to flight arrivals and departures, and that British High Commission staff do not travel the road route after dark.
The Government of Canada says the rainy season runs from May to November, with seasonal flooding, mudslides and landslides that can make roads impassable.
The UK Foreign Office says you must have a certificate proving yellow fever vaccination to enter Sierra Leone.

The US dollar and the euro are the easiest currencies to exchange, according to the Government of Canada; use banks or official exchange offices. The Bank of Sierra Leone removed three zeros from the leone in its redenomination (the new leone, SLE).

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Sierra Leone?
faq.answer: ECOWAS citizens enter visa-free, and so do citizens of Bahamas, Barbados, Botswana, Eswatini, Fiji, Jamaica, Kenya, Lesotho, Malawi, Malaysia, Mauritius, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Singapore, Sri Lanka and Trinidad and Tobago, for whom the official eVisa portal states that no visa is required. Almost everyone else can get a visa on arrival at Lungi airport and other entry points for USD 80 in cash, or apply in advance through the official eVisa portal, evisa.sl, where African Union passport holders pay USD 25.

faq.question: How much is the Sierra Leone visa on arrival?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says USD 80, paid in cash in US dollars. African Union nationals pay USD 25 for the e-Visa on evisa.sl; no official source we could read says whether that reduced rate also applies at the border. Citizens of Botswana, Eswatini, Kenya, Lesotho, Malawi and Mauritius need no visa at all.

faq.question: Does Sierra Leone have an eVisa?
faq.answer: Yes — the official Government of Sierra Leone portal at evisa.sl issues e-visas ahead of travel, with fees tiered by nationality; the portal says an approved visa is issued on arrival at the airport or border.

faq.question: Is yellow fever vaccination required for Sierra Leone?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK Foreign Office says you must have a certificate proving yellow fever vaccination to enter Sierra Leone.

faq.question: Is Sierra Leone safe to visit?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says the political situation has improved since the civil war ended in 2002, but it can change and protests can turn violent, so avoid political gatherings and follow any curfews. It reports robberies of British nationals, sometimes at knifepoint, in parts of Freetown and at peninsula beach resorts, and says serious road accidents are common.
